say: 1961-1964 'Chicken War': European countries (France, West Germany, then the EEC) raised tariffs on cheap US chicken; President Johnson answered with a 25% tariff on light trucks (plus potato starch, dextrin, brandy), proclaimed Dec 1963, effective January 1964. Still in force today.
Cargo vans / light trucks: 25% duty; passenger vehicles: 2.5% duty.
First-generation Transit Connects for the US were built in Turkey (Ford Otosan) and shipped with rear seats, seat belts and rear windows so they were declared as passenger vehicles.
At a contractor's facility in the Port of Baltimore the rear seats were removed and the rear window glass replaced with metal panels before the vans went to dealers as cargo vans.
check: auto-confirmed 2026-11-11 by fact_check.py (2+ sites, see review/fact_check.md)

check_was: manual: sources disagree on what happened to the seats (Wikipedia: shredded and recycled in Ohio; TTAC 2013: saved to sell as an option), so the script only says they were pulled out

say: In a January 30, 2013 ruling, US Customs (CBP) decided the Transit Connect is a commercial (cargo) vehicle, and called the process an attempt to 'manipulate the tariff schedule'.
Ford sued; on June 29, 2020 the US Supreme Court declined to hear Ford's appeal, leaving the cargo-van ruling in place.
March 11, 2024: Ford agreed to pay $365 million to the US to settle (DOJ: one of the largest customs penalty settlements in recent US history); Ford admitted no liability.
